records.title: DISCLOSE Act of 2026 · S. 3991
records.summary: Introduced legislation proposing additional reporting of campaign-related disbursements, safeguards around foreign funds, and ad disclaimers.
records.caveat: The introduced text is not enacted law. Ad disclaimers are not equivalent to a complete online advertising archive; this record supports only part of the reform concept.

records.title: DISCLOSE Act of 2026 · H.R. 7802
records.summary: House companion proposal for additional election-spending disclosure by organizations.
records.caveat: Original introduction documented; current stage should be checked against Congress.gov before any claim about present legislative action. Not enacted nationwide law.

records.title: Stop Insider Trading Act · H.R. 7008
records.summary: The House passed the bill on July 22, 2026. On September 30, the Senate rejected cloture on a motion to proceed, so the bill did not advance through that procedural step.
records.caveat: The bill does not necessarily match a universal ban on ownership or trading. The Senate vote was procedural, not a Senate final-passage vote; no enacted stock-trading ban is established by this record.

records.title: ETHICS Act · H.R. 4890
records.summary: Proposed restrictions on congressional stock ownership and trading for members and certain family members.
records.caveat: Introduced version, not a verified enactment or final legislative disposition.

records.title: Redistricting Reform Act of 2025 · H.R. 5449
records.summary: Proposes requiring states to use independent redistricting commissions for congressional maps.
records.caveat: Federal proposal at introduction stage in the cited government publication; not evidence that every state already uses a commission.

records.title: Fair Representation Act · H.R. 4632
records.summary: Proposes ranked-choice elections, multi-member congressional districts, and nonpartisan redistricting criteria.
records.caveat: The bill's system is broader than ranked-choice voting alone, and nonpartisan criteria do not automatically mean an independent commission.

records.title: Ranked Choice Voting Act · H.R. 6589
records.summary: Proposes ranked-choice voting for elections to the U.S. House and Senate.
records.caveat: An introduced bill is not evidence that ranked-choice voting has been adopted nationwide.

records.title: Make Elections Great Again Act · H.R. 7300
records.summary: Includes a proposal to prohibit ranked-choice voting in federal elections, providing a contrasting legislative approach.
records.caveat: The measure contains numerous other provisions; this card refers only to its ranked-choice-voting restriction. Introduced text, not verified enactment.

records.title: Protecting Our Democracy Act · S. 2838
records.summary: Includes a title on improving whistleblower protections and other governmental accountability provisions.
records.caveat: Its whistleblower title is not a verified enactment of campaign-vendor award protections, and the bill's many other provisions are not scored here.

records.title: FEC enforcement · PacMar Technologies, MUR 7690
records.summary: FEC records report a $325,000 conciliation penalty for PacMar Technologies LLC involving federal-contractor and name-of-another contribution provisions.
records.caveat: The penalty applies to PacMar, not automatically to other respondents. The FEC dismissed or took no further action on certain other allegations. This is a documented enforcement case, not evidence about unrelated donors, politicians, or bills.

records.title: New York City small-donor matching, 2025 rules
records.summary: The NYC Campaign Finance Board offers an 8:1 public match for qualifying residents' contributions, within office-specific limits, eligibility thresholds and caps.
records.caveat: A candidate's amount claimed for matching is not proof of the amount of public funds paid. Program rules and eligible amounts differ by office.

records.title: Seattle democracy vouchers · special election rules
records.summary: For the 2026 City Council District 5 special election, eligible District 5 residents receive two $50 vouchers. Regular 2027 elections return to four $25 vouchers for eligible residents citywide.
records.caveat: The 2026 district-specific exception must not be presented as an annual nationwide $100 entitlement. Program eligibility is broader than registered voters alone.

records.title: California's redistricting commission and temporary congressional exception
records.summary: The Citizens Redistricting Commission draws California's state legislative maps. Proposition 50 temporarily substitutes legislatively drawn congressional maps for 2026–2030, illustrating the importance of checking election and map year.
records.caveat: California is not a pure independent-commission example for 2026 congressional maps. The current-state map exceptions are essential for accurate comparisons.

records.title: Maine ranked-choice voting in practice
records.summary: Maine applies ranked-choice voting to state-level primaries and federal general elections under specified conditions; state general elections are not all ranked-choice contests.
records.caveat: A program's existence alone does not establish that it improves competition or turnout; those outcomes require separately matched comparative research.

records.title: FEC six-member commission structure
records.summary: Federal law provides for six commissioners; four affirmative votes are generally required for official FEC actions.
records.caveat: This describes current governance, not proof that a different number of commissioners would resolve enforcement delays.

records.title: Existing expedited federal independent-expenditure reporting
records.summary: Qualifying independent expenditures already require certain 24- and 48-hour reports depending on timing and thresholds.
records.caveat: This is not a universal 24- to 48-hour rule for all donations above $200.

votes.question: On passage
votes.caveat: Recorded passage of the House text. Not proof it became law.

votes.question: Cloture on motion to proceed
votes.caveat: Procedural vote to advance consideration, NOT a Senate final passage vote. Individual senator votes are available at the linked official roll call.

financialContext.label: FEC sampled committee receipts
financialContext.scope: Top-dollar bounded sample from selected committees; may contain unreconciled amendments. NOT a national total.

financialContext.label: IRS outbound nonprofit grants
financialContext.scope: Outbound organizational grants; NOT campaign donations, documented lobbying payments or original dark-money donors.

financialContext.label: NYC campaign finance analysis
financialContext.scope: Candidate/district/source-variant rows; matching CLAIMS are not disbursements and rows are not safe to sum across variants.

limitations: This is a small reviewed illustrative sample, not a census of all introduced legislation or votes.
Bill-version dates identify published source actions; another legislative action may have occurred later.
Senate procedural votes are not final-passage votes. A vote for or against a bill does not establish motivation.
Records share a reform topic, not a proven donor-to-legislator relationship or causal influence.
FEC receipt-side rows may be selected or amendment-unreconciled; do not sum as all federal campaign spending.
IRS grants have unverified political purpose and do not expose original hidden donors.
NYC matching claims do not establish awarded payments. No individual donor data is imported.
